title: Metric coefficients in a chart and coordinate singularities
description: Components g_ij = g(∂_i, ∂_j) of a Riemannian metric in a chart, the tensor transformation law under change of coordinates, induced metrics computed from a parametrisation via the ambient inner product, and the distinction between a degenerate coordinate expression (where a parametrisation fails to be a chart) and a genuine geometric singularity.

title: Isometries, conformal maps and model spaces
description: Isometric and conformal maps, the isometry group, Riemannian homogeneous spaces, and the standard models: Euclidean space, round spheres (in spherical and stereographic coordinates), hyperbolic space and Lie groups with left-invariant metrics.

title: Levi-Civita connection and Christoffel symbols
description: Connections on vector bundles, torsion, metric compatibility, the Koszul formula and the fundamental theorem of Riemannian geometry, Christoffel symbols in a chart and their non-tensorial transformation, the tangential connection of a submanifold.

title: Riemannian distance and completeness
description: Arc length and the distance function, the induced metric-space topology, minimising curves and geodesics, the exponential map and normal neighbourhoods, geodesic completeness and the Hopf–Rinow theorem.

title: Riemannian submanifolds and the second fundamental form
description: Normal bundle, second fundamental form, the Gauss equation relating intrinsic and ambient curvature, totally geodesic and minimal submanifolds, hypersurfaces and the shape operator.

title: Jacobi fields and comparison theorems
description: Variations through geodesics, the Jacobi equation, conjugate points, the second variation formula and comparison of distances and Jacobi fields with constant-curvature models.

title: The Gauss–Bonnet theorem
description: Gaussian curvature of surfaces, the local Gauss–Bonnet formula and the global theorem relating total curvature to the Euler characteristic.

title: Curvature and topology
description: Spaces of constant curvature and their classification, the Cartan–Hadamard theorem for nonpositive curvature and Myers's theorem for positive Ricci curvature as examples of local-to-global results.
